A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite restructuring and changed pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on text-to-image, layout, molecule, and unconditional image generation in Section 6 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: GRAFT, P-GRAFT, inverse noise correction, and Algorithms 1–7 retain the same procedures. The new final-distribution analysis describes the existing model-switching procedure without modifying it.

E1.justification: Both versions use GenAI-Bench, T2ICompBench++, GenEval, PubLayNet, QM9, CelebA-HQ, and LSUN-Church for the same tasks and scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SDv2, SDXL-Base, and DDPO. Appendix E.3 retains the same DDPO variants and PRDP trial, while Figure 8 retains the LDM-4/LDM-8 reference comparisons.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, sampling schedules, Top-K configurations, model sizes, and training budgets match. Tables 13–19 and the settings in Appendices E–G contain no substantive protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same Top-K, LoRA-rank, reverse-stitching, conditional-variance, molecule de-duplication, and ReDeNoise ablations, together with the same compute analyses and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: The same ± reporting and the molecule conditional-variance experiment using 100 rollouts and 1,000 repetitions are retained. Run counts, seed disclosures, and statistical reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–21 and the plotted and qualitative outcomes match. For example, P-GRAFT(0.25N) retains 71.94±0.14 on GenAI-Bench in Table 2 and 92.61±0.13 molecule stability in Table 4.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.3.1 derives the final stitched distribution. For acceptance depending only on reward and its empirical CDF, it establishes two special cases: independent rewards produce no tilt, while rewards determined by the intermediate state reproduce GRAFT. Existing theorems and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 lists GRS/GRAFT unification and its KL equivalence as contribution (a). v3 recasts the equivalences as known results supporting the work, foregrounding P-GRAFT and inverse noise correction. The principal method and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3.1 newly explains when intermediate shaping leaves the final distribution unchanged or matches GRAFT, and notes the lack of a general explicit solution. These add substantive qualifications to the interpretation of the unchanged sampling procedure.

D1.justification: The LoRA and noise-schedule instructions, baseline implementation link, training hyperparameters, inverse-noise training details, and LSUN-Church stabilization procedure are retained. Typographical corrections and footnote renumbering add no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The introduction more explicitly acknowledges established rejection-sampling/KL equivalences and positions them as background for the proposed contributions. The cited works and substantive related-work coverage in Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites portions of the abstract, introduction, and inverse-noise motivation, and incorporates the former standalone GRAFT section into an expanded Preliminaries section. Most exposition and appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a document-wide ICLR layout with a redesigned title/author block, different headers and heading typography, narrower text, and resized or repositioned algorithms, tables, plots, and image grids. The underlying figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix D.3.1 fills a limited explanatory gap between intermediate distribution shaping and final sampling, including useful special-case boundaries. The introduction also distinguishes established equivalences from the proposed contributions more clearly. These improve theoretical transparency and positioning while the methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
